newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Bid to consider U.N. seat for Taiwan blocked again.
newsitem.headline: Bid to consider U.N. seat for Taiwan blocked again.

text.p: For the fourth year in a row, China and its supporters blocked an attempt on Wednesday to get the General Assembly to consider U.N. membership for Taiwan.

As in previous years, the move to inscribe the issue on the agenda, sponsored by 17 mostly Caribbean, Central American and African countries, was defeated without a vote in the Assembly's steering committee.
The 28-member committee acted after the proposal was introduced by the representative of the Solomon Islands and strongly opposed by China's ambassador.

A large number of other envoys, including non-members of the committee, also spoke, with 38 opposing the item and 17 supporting it in the only debate sparked by any of the more than 160 proposed agenda items.

When China's Nationalist government retreated to Taiwan in 1949 after defeat by the Communists in a civil war, it continued to hold China's U.N. seat. But it was expelled by the Assembly in 1971 and the seat given to Beijing, which considers Taiwan a renegade province.

China regards any bid to give the island U.N. membership as an intolerable encroachment on its sovereignty and interference in its internal affairs, and suggests the sponsors are motivated by economic inducements.
